newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan's Bashir off to S.Africa for Mandela talks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan's Bashir off to S.Africa for Mandela talks.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir flew to South Africa on Monday for talks with President Nelson Mandela on ways to end 14 years of civil war in southern Sudan, officials and state media said.
Mandela has tried over the past few months to mediate in the fighting which has pitted Christian, animist rebels in the south against the Moslem, Arab north.

"The visit comes within the context of supporting government efforts to achieve peace," the government al-Anbaa newspaper quoted Sudanese First Vice President Lieutenant-General Al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh as saying.
Omdurman state radio said Bashir's visit was in response to an invitation from Mandela.
The South African leader has in the past invited both Bashir and John Garang, the leader of the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) to South Africa for talks with him on ways to end the war.
Garang's SPLA has rejected a peace deal struck earlier this year between the government and other southern rebel groups.
Mandela has played the role of peace broker several times since he emerged in 1990 from a quarter-of-a-century in jail to lead South Africa from apartheid to democracy.

Alone or in concert with other southern African leaders, Mandela has contributed to peacemaking missions in Angola, Algeria, Lesotho, Swaziland, Burundi, Nigeria and Zaire, which is now known as the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
